title: Capacity and Margin
scenario: A manufacturer has idle capacity. Product X sells for $90, variable cost is $52, and requires 2 machine hours. Product Y sells for $120, variable cost is $72, and requires 3 machine hours. Machine time is constrained.

questions.q: Which product has the higher contribution margin per unit?
questions.explanation: X contributes $38; Y contributes $48 per unit.

questions.q: Which product has the higher contribution margin per machine hour?
questions.explanation: X: $38/2=$19 per hour; Y: $48/3=$16 per hour.

title: Project Evaluation
scenario: A company is evaluating a project requiring $200,000 initially. Expected annual after-tax cash inflows are $80,000 for three years. Required return is 10%. Ignore salvage value.

questions.q: Ignoring discounting, what is simple payback?
Why is NPV preferred over simple payback for value-creation decisions?

choices.B: NPV incorporates time value of money

questions.explanation: NPV discounts future cash flows using the required return.

title: Flexible Budget Review
scenario: A service company prepared a monthly static budget for 10,000 service hours. Budgeted variable operating costs are $18 per hour and budgeted fixed operating costs are $90,000. Actual activity was 12,000 hours and actual operating costs were $315,000.

questions.q: What is the flexible-budget operating cost for 12,000 hours?
Compared with the flexible budget, actual operating costs produced what variance?
questions.explanation: Actual $315,000 minus flexible budget $306,000 equals a $9,000 unfavorable variance.

title: Special Order Decision
scenario: A company has unused production capacity. A customer offers to buy 4,000 units for $42 each. Variable manufacturing cost is $27 per unit, and the special order would add $3 per unit of shipping cost. No fixed costs would change, and accepting the order would not reduce normal sales.

questions.q: What is the incremental contribution per special-order unit?
questions.explanation: Incremental revenue $42 less variable manufacturing $27 and shipping $3 equals $12 per unit.
